raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
Stack from [ghstack](https://github.com/ezyang/ghstack/tree/0.15.0) (oldest at bottom):
* __->__ #5792

Add Profiler.Config.kernel_span_ring: every training step, each rank records
every CUDA kernel's GPU start/end time, CUDA graph node id and stream with a
Cuspy observer, files the kernels into training steps, and writes them every
steps_per_file steps (default 100) to a per-rank .npz, deleting the oldest files
written by the run beyond num_steps_retained (default 1000). A slow step can then
be inspected after the fact without having scheduled a profiling window for it.

Kernels are named from the CUDA graph nodes they replay: a graph instantiate
hook records each node's kernel name, launch geometry and graph annotations
(mark_kernels regions, c10d collective metadata) once per graph, and each file
embeds the table for the graphs its steps ran. scripts/kernel_span_ring_to_trace.py
joins kernels to that table and writes a Chrome/Perfetto trace for chosen steps
and ranks.

- KernelSpanRecorder runs from Profiler.step() on the training thread: record
  the step's host end time, flush CUPTI without a device sync, and cut the
  delivered kernels (kept sorted by start time) at the end of every step for
  which a later kernel has arrived. _KernelSpanRing buffers finished steps,
  writes a file every steps_per_file steps and evicts old files.
- Requires accelerator graphs (validated in TrainingEngine.Config) and CUDA
  graph node ids (CUDA 13.1+ driver or cuda-compat). Kineto windowed profiling
  cannot run alongside it; Cuspy windowed profiling can, with graph annotations
  keyed by exec-graph node id.
- Rename _cuspy_unavailable_reasons to cuspy_unavailable_reasons, now used
  from kernel_span_ring.py.

## Cost

4x GB300, FSDP over 4 GPUs, CUDA graphs, cuda-compat 13.1. Baseline and
kernel_span_ring runs alternated, 2 rounds each. Llama 3 8B: seq 8192, 60 steps,
medians over steps 21-60. Qwen3 32B: seq 4096, full activation recompute, 40
steps, medians over steps 16-40. Both runs are GPU-bound. steps_per_file=20
so files are written inside the measured window (5x more often than the
default).

Performance:

| Model (kernels/step) | Round | Step time, baseline | Step time, ring | Change | Tokens/s/GPU, baseline | Tokens/s/GPU, ring |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Llama 3 8B (2.3k) | 1 | 377.4 ms | 377.7 ms | +0.1% | 21,802 | 21,662 |
| Llama 3 8B (2.3k) | 2 | 377.7 ms | 382.6 ms | +1.3% | 21,732 | 20,760 |
| Qwen3 32B (5.4k) | 1 | 2,963.0 ms | 2,969.1 ms | +0.2% | 5,528 | 5,514 |
| Qwen3 32B (5.4k) | 2 | 2,963.1 ms | 2,973.5 ms | +0.35% | 5,524 | 5,512 |

Tokens/s is averaged over the logged steps in the window (every 10 steps), so
it is noisier than the median step time.

Memory and disk, per rank:

| Model | GPU peak reserved, baseline -> ring | Host peak RSS, baseline -> ring | Disk per step (steps_per_file=100) | Disk at default retention (1000 steps) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Llama 3 8B | 61.33 -> 61.33 GiB | 3.49 -> 3.52 GiB | 81 KB | ~81 MB |
| Qwen3 32B | 145.28 -> 145.28 GiB | 3.66-3.67 -> 3.71 GiB | 188 KB | ~188 MB |

Host RSS was sampled every 2 s from each training process. Disk per step
includes the node table, which is stored once per file (0.6 MB for 8B, 1.5 MB
for 32B).

Time taken:

| Model | Recorder step(), median per step | Recorder step(), max (includes file writes) | Write one 100-step file | Convert 1 step x 4 ranks | Convert 10 steps x 4 ranks |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Llama 3 8B | 2.8-3.5 ms | 12.6-43.0 ms | 3.9 ms (8.1 MB) | 2.3 s (0.6 GB peak) | 4.6 s (0.6 GB peak) |
| Qwen3 32B | 5.3 ms | 24.5-24.9 ms | 8.5 ms (18.8 MB) | 2.7 s (0.6 GB peak) | 8.2 s (0.7 GB peak) |

The recorder runs on the host while it waits on the GPU, so its time is mostly
hidden in GPU-bound steps. File write times are page-cache writes to local disk,
measured by re-saving the run's files. Conversion runs offline, off the
training machines.

Numerics: loss and grad_norm match the baseline for 30 steps of the llama3
debug model (seed 42, deterministic, flex attention, 2 GPUs).

@@ -0,0 +1,192 @@
+# Copyright (c) Meta Platforms, Inc. and affiliates.
+# All rights reserved.
+#
+# This source code is licensed under the BSD-style license found in the
+# LICENSE file in the root directory of this source tree.
+
+"""Convert kernel span ring steps into a Chrome trace for Perfetto.
+
+Reads the step files ``Profiler.Config.kernel_span_ring`` writes (see
+``torchtitan/observability/kernel_span_ring.py``) and joins each kernel span to
+its CUDA graph node, so slices carry the kernel name and the node's graph
+annotations. Ranks become processes and CUDA streams become threads; each step
+also gets a slice on a ``steps`` track spanning its kernels.
+
+Example::
+
+    python scripts/kernel_span_ring_to_trace.py \\
+        outputs/profiling/kernel_span_ring --steps 150-152 --ranks 0,1 \\
+        --output trace.json.gz
+
+Open the output in https://ui.perfetto.dev.
+"""
+
+import argparse
+import glob
+import gzip
+import json
+import os
+import re
+
+import numpy as np
+
+_STEPS_FILE_RE = re.compile(r"steps_(\d+)_(\d+)\.npz$")
+_RANK_DIR_RE = re.compile(r"rank(\d+)$")
+# Thread id for the per-rank track of step slices; CUDA stream ids are small.
+_STEPS_TID = -1
+
+
+def _parse_int_list(spec: str) -> list[int]:
+    """Parse ``"3,5-7"`` into ``[3, 5, 6, 7]``."""
+    values: list[int] = []
+    for part in spec.split(","):
+        first, _, last = part.partition("-")
+        values.extend(range(int(first), int(last or first) + 1))
+    return values
+
+
+def _demangle(name: str) -> str:
+    try:
+        from torch._C import _demangle as demangle
+    except ImportError:
+        return name
+    return demangle(name)
+
+
+def _rank_dirs(ring_dir: str, ranks: list[int] | None) -> dict[int, str]:
+    found = {}
+    for path in glob.glob(os.path.join(ring_dir, "rank*")):
+        if (match := _RANK_DIR_RE.search(path)) and os.path.isdir(path):
+            found[int(match.group(1))] = path
+    if ranks is None:
+        return dict(sorted(found.items()))
+    missing = [rank for rank in ranks if rank not in found]
+    if missing:
+        raise ValueError(f"no rank directories for ranks {missing} under {ring_dir}")
+    return {rank: found[rank] for rank in ranks}
+
+
+def _rank_events(rank: int, rank_dir: str, steps: set[int]) -> tuple[list, set[int]]:
+    """Return the trace events for ``steps`` on one rank, and the steps found."""
+    events: list[dict] = [
+        {
+            "ph": "M",
+            "name": "process_name",
+            "pid": rank,
+            "args": {"name": f"rank {rank}"},
+        },
+        {
+            "ph": "M",
+            "name": "thread_name",
+            "pid": rank,
+            "tid": _STEPS_TID,
+            "args": {"name": "steps"},
+        },
+    ]
+    found: set[int] = set()
+    streams: set[int] = set()
+    num_unnamed = 0
+    for path in sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(rank_dir, "steps_*.npz"))):
+        match = _STEPS_FILE_RE.search(path)
+        assert match is not None
+        first_step, last_step = int(match.group(1)), int(match.group(2))
+        if not any(first_step <= step <= last_step for step in steps):
+            continue
+        data = np.load(path)
+        node_table = json.loads(data["node_table"].tobytes())
+        offsets = data["step_offsets"]
+        for i, step in enumerate(data["steps"].tolist()):
+            if step not in steps:
+                continue
+            found.add(step)
+            rows = slice(offsets[i], offsets[i + 1])
+            node_ids = data["graph_node_id"][rows].tolist()
+            starts = data["start_ns"][rows].tolist()
+            ends = data["end_ns"][rows].tolist()
+            stream_ids = data["stream_id"][rows].tolist()
+            for node_id, start, end, stream in zip(node_ids, starts, ends, stream_ids):
+                streams.add(stream)
+                node = node_table.get(str(node_id)) if node_id else None
+                args: dict = {"graph_node_id": node_id}
+                if node is None:
+                    name = "eager kernel" if node_id == 0 else "unknown graph node"
+                    num_unnamed += node_id != 0
+                else:
+                    name = _demangle(node["kernel_name"] or node["node_type"])
+                    if node["grid"] is not None:
+                        args["grid"], args["block"] = node["grid"], node["block"]
+                    for annotation in node["annotations"] or []:
+                        if isinstance(annotation, dict):
+                            args.update(annotation)
+                events.append(
+                    {
+                        "ph": "X",
+                        "cat": "kernel",
+                        "name": name,
+                        "pid": rank,
+                        "tid": stream,
+                        "ts": start / 1e3,
+                        "dur": (end - start) / 1e3,
+                        "args": args,
+                    }
+                )
+            if starts:
+                events.append(
+                    {
+                        "ph": "X",
+                        "cat": "step",
+                        "name": f"step {step}",
+                        "pid": rank,
+                        "tid": _STEPS_TID,
+                        "ts": min(starts) / 1e3,
+                        "dur": (max(ends) - min(starts)) / 1e3,
+                        "args": {"num_kernels": len(starts)},
+                    }
+                )
+    events.extend(
+        {
+            "ph": "M",
+            "name": "thread_name",
+            "pid": rank,
+            "tid": stream,
+            "args": {"name": f"stream {stream}"},
+        }
+        for stream in sorted(streams)
+    )
+    if num_unnamed:
+        print(
+            f"rank {rank}: {num_unnamed} graph kernel spans have no node table entry "
+            "(their graph was instantiated before the recorder started)"
+        )
+    return events, found
+
+
+def main() -> None:
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n\n")[0])
+    parser.add_argument("ring_dir", help="kernel span ring folder holding rank*/ dirs")
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--steps", required=True, help='steps to convert, e.g. "150-152,160"'
+    )
+    parser.add_argument("--ranks", help='ranks to include, e.g. "0-3"; default all')
+    parser.add_argument("--output", required=True, help="output .json or .json.gz path")
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+
+    steps = set(_parse_int_list(args.steps))
+    ranks = None if args.ranks is None else _parse_int_list(args.ranks)
+    events: list[dict] = []
+    for rank, rank_dir in _rank_dirs(args.ring_dir, ranks).items():
+        rank_events, found = _rank_events(rank, rank_dir, steps)
+        if missing := sorted(steps - found):
+            print(
+                f"rank {rank}: steps {missing} are not in the ring (evicted or not reached)"
+            )
+        events.extend(rank_events)
+
+    opener = gzip.open if args.output.endswith(".gz") else open
+    with opener(args.output, "wt") as f:
+        json.dump({"traceEvents": events, "displayTimeUnit": "ms"}, f)
+    print(f"wrote {sum(e['ph'] == 'X' for e in events)} slices to {args.output}")
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

@@ -85,3 +85,56 @@ print(sorted(supported_metrics()))  # e.g. "sm__cycles_active" -> "sm__cycles_ac
 The trace gets the PM samples still in the buffer when profiling ends. If the warmup and active steps together take longer than the lookback window, the earliest samples are dropped.
 
 The sample buffer is held in process memory while profiling, not written to the trace. CUPTI stores raw hardware counters for every sample (several KB each, depending on the metrics), so it grows with lookback / interval: e.g. about 1.1 GiB at 100 s / 2 ms with 7 metrics.
+
+## Always-on kernel spans
+
+`Profiler.Config.kernel_span_ring` records every CUDA kernel's GPU start and end
+time on every training step with Cuspy, so a slow step can be inspected after the
+fact without having scheduled a profiling window for it. Each rank keeps the most
+recent `num_steps_retained` steps (default 1000) on disk:
+
+```python
+from torchtitan.observability.profiler import KernelSpanRingConfig
+
+config.profiler.kernel_span_ring = KernelSpanRingConfig(num_steps_retained=1000)
+```
+
+```
+<dump_folder>/profiling/kernel_span_ring/
+  rank0/
+    steps_000000000901_000000001000.npz   # one file per steps_per_file (100) steps, oldest deleted first
+    steps_000000001001_000000001100.npz
+  rank1/
+    ...
+```
+
+Kernels are named from the CUDA graph nodes they were replayed from, so this
+requires accelerator graphs (the default). Each file carries the kernel names and
+graph annotations (`mark_kernels` regions, c10d collective metadata) of the graphs
+its steps ran; eager kernels outside graphs are recorded without names. See
+[`kernel_span_ring.py`](kernel_span_ring.py) for the file format.
+
+Requirements are the Cuspy ones above, plus CUDA graph node ids: a CUDA 13.1 or
+newer driver, or cuda-compat 13.1 or newer on `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` (see
+`torch.cuda.graph_annotations.is_available`).
+
+Convert steps into a Chrome trace and open it in <https://ui.perfetto.dev>:
+
+```bash
+python scripts/kernel_span_ring_to_trace.py \
+    outputs/profiling/kernel_span_ring --steps 1050-1052 --ranks 0-3 \
+    --output trace.json.gz
+```
+
+Ranks become processes and CUDA streams become tracks, with a `steps` track
+marking each step's kernels.
+
+A step holds the kernels that started on the GPU between the host-side ends of
+the previous step and this one. Training only syncs the host with the GPU on
+logging steps, so when the host runs ahead of the GPU, a step can hold the tail of
+earlier steps. Steps buffered since the last file are lost if the process is
+killed without a clean shutdown.
+
+Measured on 4 GB300s with FSDP and CUDA graphs, collection and writing cost 0.4%
+of step time for Llama 3 8B (about 2,300 kernels per step) and under 0.5% for
+Qwen3 32B (about 5,400 kernels per step, about 190 KB per step on disk).

+# Copyright (c) Meta Platforms, Inc. and affiliates.
+# All rights reserved.
+#
+# This source code is licensed under the BSD-style license found in the
+# LICENSE file in the root directory of this source tree.
+
+"""Always-on recording of every CUDA kernel's GPU start and end time, kept per
+training step in a rolling set of files on disk.
+
+How data flows, per rank:
+
+    CUPTI --flush--> unfiled kernels --cut at step ends--> finished steps
+                                                                |
+                                       every steps_per_file steps, write one file
+                                                                |
+                                         files on disk, oldest deleted first
+
+- KernelSpanRecorder receives kernel records from CUPTI and works out which
+  training step each kernel belongs to.
+- _KernelSpanRing buffers finished steps, writes them to files, and deletes old
+  files so that about num_steps_retained steps stay on disk.
+
+Each file, named steps_<first step>_<last step>.npz, holds one row per kernel:
+its CUDA graph node id (0 for kernels launched outside CUDA graphs), GPU start
+and end time (unix nanoseconds) and CUDA stream. Kernels are grouped by step;
+step_offsets marks where each step's rows begin. The file also stores a node
+table, recorded when each CUDA graph was instantiated, that maps graph node ids
+to kernel names and graph annotations (mark_kernels regions, c10d collective
+metadata). Node ids are only meaningful within one process, so every file
+carries its own table. scripts/kernel_span_ring_to_trace.py turns chosen steps
+into a Chrome/Perfetto trace.
+
+Caveats: steps are cut at the moment each step ends on the host. The host
+usually runs ahead of the GPU, so a step can include the tail of earlier steps.
+Steps not yet written to a file are lost if the process is killed.
+
+Imported lazily by torchtitan.observability.profiler.Profiler, since it needs
+Cuspy and the cupti-python package.
+"""
+
+import json
+import os
+from collections import deque
+from typing import Any
+
+import numpy as np
+import torch
+
+# TODO: these are private torch APIs; move to a public per-step span observer once
+# torch exposes one.
+from cupti.cupti import ActivityKind
+from torch.profiler._cuspy.observers.node_timer import NodeTimerObserver
+
+from torchtitan.observability.profiler import (
+    cuspy_unavailable_reasons,
+    CuspyProfilerConfig,
+)
+
+STEPS_FILE = "steps_{first_step:012d}_{last_step:012d}.npz"
+
+# One row per kernel. Times are unix nanoseconds; graph_node_id is 0 for eager
+# kernels.
+_SPAN_DTYPE = np.dtype(
+    [
+        ("graph_node_id", "<u8"),
+        ("start_ns", "<i8"),
+        ("end_ns", "<i8"),
+        ("stream_id", "<u8"),
+    ]
+)
+
+
+class KernelSpanRecorder(NodeTimerObserver):
+    """Receives kernel records from CUPTI and files each kernel into the training
+    step it ran in.
+
+    CUPTI records every kernel the GPU runs, but hands the records over late and
+    in batches that don't line up with steps: the host queues work ahead of the
+    GPU, so when a step ends on the host, some of its kernels haven't run or
+    haven't been reported yet.
+
+    The recorder keeps two things in memory:
+
+    - step ends: for each step that has ended but isn't finished yet, the time it
+      ended on the host. step() adds one per training step.
+    - unfiled kernels: kernels CUPTI has reported that aren't assigned to a step
+      yet, sorted by start time.
+
+    Each step() call records the step's end, flushes CUPTI (without a device
+    sync) to collect newly reported kernels, and cuts the unfiled kernels at the
+    step ends of every finished step (see _close_steps). Finished steps go to a
+    _KernelSpanRing, which writes them to disk. Kernels are named from the CUDA
+    graph nodes they ran as, so training must run in CUDA graphs; kernels
+    launched outside graphs are recorded without names.
+
+    Args:
+        ring_dir: Directory for this rank's step files. Files already there (e.g.
+            from before a restart) are left alone and never deleted.
+        global_step: The last completed training step; the first :meth:`step`
+            call ends step ``global_step + 1``.
+        num_steps_retained: Number of steps to keep on disk, rounded up to whole
+            files.
+        steps_per_file: Number of complete steps written per file.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        ring_dir: str,
+        *,
+        global_step: int,
+        num_steps_retained: int,
+        steps_per_file: int,
+    ) -> None:
+        if not torch.cuda.is_available():
+            raise ValueError(
+                "profiler.kernel_span_ring is set, but no CUDA device is available."
+            )
+        if reasons := cuspy_unavailable_reasons(CuspyProfilerConfig()):
+            raise ValueError(
+                "profiler.kernel_span_ring is set, but Cuspy cannot run here:\n  - "
+                + "\n  - ".join(reasons)
